I will almost be 18 soon and I've been wanting to get a tattoo since I was 14. I saw this piece long time ago and my love for it still there. Now, I have a couple questions.

Here is the piece I want in the exact location. Tattoo

  • How much would it hurt in that area? (I'm kinda sensitive to pain, but I'd pull through.)
  • I eventually want to get a sleeve later, so what arm should I put the piece on. (I am right handed...I don't know if that helps with anything lol.)
  • Do tattoo places reuse needles. My dad's best friend got ill and died because his tattoo artist reused a needle, so I kinda have this fear now.
  • Could a tattoo artist perfectly replicate the piece above and where would I find a skilled artist in California?
  • I will be attending college and working as a computer technician during my time at college, so would having a tattoo that is visible make me look bad in front of my professors/boss or have a "badboy" vibe in front of my peers (not that I would want that).
  • If a tattoo ever got scratched or bitten by a dog for example, would it ruin the piece forever or could it be fixed?
I can't really help you in most parts, but I would suggest getting a tattoo where it can be easily hidden. Employers would look at that tattoo and form first impressions that might not be the best.
Ask your tattoo artist. Google tattoo shops, go to them. Invest your time and money in your ink.

First off, I know you didn't ask this and if you're dead set on it I can't change your mind, but I'd strongly recommend not straight up copying someone else's tattoo. By all means, get an "inspired by" piece done in the same style, but don't get the exact same tattoo that someone else already has (probably more than one person since that picture is all over the internet). You can do better than that. Find a good artist and have them draw up something original, for you. On to your questions:

1) It's hard to say how much it'll hurt, people are sensitive in slightly different areas and have different pain thresholds. Generally the inner forearm would be pretty pinchy but not unbearable.

2) Whichever arm you want it on. Really. Some people say it's marginally easier to heal tattoos on your non-dominant arm because you don't use it as much so it's less likely to accidentally brush off things, but I have tattoos on both arms and I really didn't notice a difference to be honest.

3) Reusing needles is a major no-no. No semi-decent studio would ever do that. It's standard practice to open the needles and tubes fresh in front of you.

4) Possibly, if you do go for an exact copy you'd want to be careful because copies are rarely as good as the originals. The quality of the photo isn't great and it's hard to see the fine lines, and some artists (not all) may no be happy directly copying another artist's work. California is a big place, if you want to narrow it down a bit (even in a PM) I'll check out some studios in your area for you.

5) Probably not, tattoos are becoming more commonplace but they are still frowned upon in some professional environments. I don't know what the dress code for computer technicians tends to be like, but if you wear long sleeves to cover it you should be fine.

6) It would depend a lot on the severity of the injury, how it heals, and the nature of the scarring, but it's really impossible to say without actually seeing what needs to be done. Usually a skilled artist can do something, whether that's fixing it up or covering it depends on what they have to work with.

I have a bunch of tattoos and I have some advice on first tattoo's. Figure out what you want, make sure it's perfect. When you are absolutely certain it is "THE ONE." Throw it out, start over with number two, because first tattoos are always a mistake! And as previously commented, start above the sleeve of a short sleeve shirt. I can still wear a short sleeve shirt and look professional. I get to choose when and where I let my freak flag fly.
